# Owned LHA reference inputs

The payloads, `Reference.java` and `author-reference/` host harness are project-authored and distributed under the repository's Apache-2.0 license. They contain no imported upstream test archives or user data. Compressed bytes are generated through public reference APIs, with additional independently authored initial-history streams. Tool source and binaries remain outside Git under `build/toolchain/` and are not runtime dependencies.

## Fixed references

- jLHA 0.0.11, original Michel Ishizuka BSD-2-Clause license, [source commit](https://github.com/umjammer/jlha/tree/0a6348d96e9bbb1ac5ee8b3f6ff1c2c75b17d0d9) `0a6348d96e9bbb1ac5ee8b3f6ff1c2c75b17d0d9`. The downloaded source zip SHA-256 is `ef9feb1c59f55aff69b00c0d69dee5edaefb45e86950a99a6728beb35e70ff3a`. Compile only its main sources/resources and the owned API harness, without importing upstream test inputs or Maven dependencies.
- Temurin OpenJDK 17.0.21+9, [official Windows x64 release](https://github.com/adoptium/temurin17-binaries/releases/tag/jdk-17.0.21%2B9). Zip SHA-256 `98518ecf554465057ee5509462631deeee374bc368c12a411d225cd29381f84b`; every extracted regular file is compared with the verified zip before compilation and execution. This is a portable test tool, without installation or system configuration changes.
- Lhasa 0.6.0, ISC, [author release](https://github.com/fragglet/lhasa/releases/tag/v0.6.0). Windows zip SHA-256 `5925e6a7b615d784e381e18240a1537d55a42cddad91d21e13c604a40974fe28`, executable SHA-256 `93cf8100eb520e49708c5076694253d52caf241d6013be4e37c11ec8e89bbe85`. Extract only owned members inside an owned temporary child directory. Windows stdout can translate line endings, so binary file contents, rather than redirected text output, are compared.
- 7-Zip 26.06, [author download](https://www.7-zip.org/download.html). The existing verified full reference executable SHA-256 is `dc0493429fe28136fcb177a0e77c9875cbb3b0bff5f2f8eeba4df302e98cef76`, and its matching `7z.dll` is `500db9eb17f3c21b729ba41dd02ecfe1823da05028c7e4ba129084cc74cc364e`. Compare complete binary stdout only for supported methods.

The original author decoder is the unmodified `dhuf.c` from [LHa for Unix](https://github.com/jca02266/lha/blob/16619b066b189ef289bb8b07b37d1c38d550da99/src/dhuf.c), commit `16619b066b189ef289bb8b07b37d1c38d550da99`, Git blob `bcb08bdccf6c6396938e3b2d9b6b032a991aa26e`, SHA-256 `99a0d828039b85dc9061b797388be3d6408094224d35d7f482122d0305a7854b`. Its original license remains applicable to that reference. The source is not redistributed here or compiled into the product. The owned C files only provide bounded source bits, independent output history and a controlled host for raw decoding and test-only encoder state. Stress generation includes the unmodified source only inside the reference build, invoking its original encoder/growth helpers; no such source or algorithm state enters a product target. GCC 13.2.0 under the existing Strawberry Perl 5.42.3.1 reference toolchain has executable SHA-256 `34a92e71f6814bd936135d0bd82b80b63daaf445791bba4a6bba93075235e8a4`. Source, compiler and generated executable remain under `build/toolchain/`; the generator verifies their admitted inputs before compilation.

The generator verifies these identities, recompiles the public API harness and compares reference output with authored payload bytes. It does not install reference code or add product dependencies. The [wire contract](../../../docs/engineering/lha-containers.md) records primary format sources and source-observation limits.

## Input definitions

`{method}-h{level}.lzh` combines methods `lh0`, `lh1`, `lh2`, `lh3`, `lh4`, `lh5`, `lh6`, `lh7`, `lzs`, `lz4`, `lz5` with header levels 0, 1, 2 and 3. Each contains `hello.bin`, the bytes `abracadabra abracadabra\n` repeated six times, timestamp 1700000000 UTC, and a declared payload CRC-16. The harness forces the named raw encoder without a Store fallback.

For the nine compressed methods, `empty`, `tail1`, `spaces`, `random` and `long` use respectively no bytes, `A`, 4096 spaces, 65000 deterministic xorshift32 high bytes, and the phrase repeated 6 × 4096 times. Xorshift starts at `0x6d2b79f5` and applies shifts 13 left, 17 right and 5 left in 32-bit arithmetic. All these cases use header level 2. Empty compressed members have zero packed bytes; they do not establish acceptance of a coded empty block.

`lh5-h2-padding.lzh` uses the same phrase with a 222-byte filename, 218 `x` bytes followed by `.bin`. Its level-2 header would otherwise be 256 bytes, so one zero padding byte makes it 257. Reference extraction uses a short owned directory under `build/` to retain the full member name within Lhasa's Windows path limit.

`lh2-unix-spaces.lzh` contains 4096 spaces, one literal followed by fifteen length-256 and one length-255 references. Its owned encoder uses public generic tree APIs while leaving an initial singleton position leaf's weight unchanged, matching original Unix LH2. Its 46-byte packed stream is independently read completely by the original author decoder. jLHA's ordinary 45-byte space stream follows the incompatible singleton update convention. The original reference exactly reads seven of the nine ordinary LH2 cases plus the dedicated Unix space and rescaling cases; it disagrees on ordinary space/long data, and jLHA disagrees on the Unix-specific case. These are explicit variant differences.

`lh2-unix-short.lzh` and `lh2-jlha-short.lzh` each begin with byte values 0–63 and then contain 33000 length-three matches. A 32-bit xorshift with the same seed/shifts above chooses each offset modulo the smaller of the current output size and 8192. Copying is overlapping and uses only already produced history. Their complete known output has 99064 bytes. Both cross character and position-model rescaling thresholds, with varying actual distances and bytes so a wrong tree cannot pass as a constant fill. The original author's private encoder and growth functions produce the Unix reference stream; the public `PostLh2Encoder` API produces the jLHA stream. Each reference completely reads its own stream and disagrees on the other. These are independent references to the Rust implementation, not product self-roundtrips.

`named-utf8.lzh` and `named-shiftjis.lzh` use public jLHA header encoding with explicit UTF-8 or Shift_JIS. Their paths are respectively `nested/资料/说明.txt` and `nested/ソフトウェアの設定/ソフトウェアの設定ファイルと日本語.txt`, retaining the phrase payload. The harness roundtrips the complete header path; Python independently splits original `0xff` dirname fields and strictly decodes each field to the expected Unicode path. jLHA and 7-Zip read the complete payload; Lhasa is not run for these two cases, recorded as null rather than unsupported.

Three wire-authored level-0 cases test initial history directly. `lh5-initial.lzh` contains one length-three distance-one command and produces three spaces. `lzs-initial.lzh` references initial absolute position zero for seventeen spaces. `lz5-initial.lzh` references position zero for eighteen bytes, thirteen zeroes and five ones. Their headers and CRCs are constructed independently of Rust.

jLHA generates and exactly rereads the 90 ordinary cases and exactly reads the LZ5 initial case and the jLHA rescaling case, plus both named cases (94 exact reads total). Its zero-filled LH5/LZS defaults disagree with the original LHa space-filled profile, so those two cases are explicitly recorded as reference disagreements. Lhasa exactly reads 75 cases and does not support LH2/LH3. 7-Zip exactly reads 40 cases including both named cases using LH0/LH4/LH5/LH6/LH7/LZ4 and rejects the other methods, the initial LH5 profile the valid level-2 padding case and all level-3 headers with a header/data error. Unsupported exit codes and initial-history disagreements are never counted as successful decoding.

These are reference capabilities, separate from Rust method admission or product support. The decoded payload and CRC must match; merely listing a method is insufficient. No claim is made for passwords, volumes, special objects, unlisted header extensions or historical repair variants. LH2 dual-variant admission requires CRC and complete candidate equality checks as specified in the wire contract.

## Reproduction and integrity

Run `python scripts/generate-lha-fixtures.py --check` with the verified references under the documented `build/toolchain/references/` subdirectories. Without `--check`, it regenerates the owned archives and compile-time fixture expectations. Actual reference results and temporary extraction files go under `build/review/format-expansion/`; the source tree contains only durable owned inputs, the harness and expectations.

For all 98 archive files sorted by UTF-8 filename, SHA-256 of the concatenation of each filename, one zero byte and its complete archive bytes is `bcb64d4be9c7d2b7cbcc364b276a3512f50b2318696bf3f837fd5c185374170e`. The generator's check mode compares every archive and the exact Rust fixture expectations. Rust primitive tests independently compare complete decoded bytes and declared CRCs; self-roundtrips are not the independent reference.
